title: COMMUNITY: COdevelopment of Microbiota and imMUNITY in intensive care
summary:
The interaction between the environment, the microbiome and the immune system of hospitalized newborns and premature infants has only been characterized to a limited extent. This is also relevant because nosocomial transmission of pathogens is a particular problem in this vulnerable patient population, as it often leads to severe infections. The project proposed here is intended to use the relocation of the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Freiburg University Medical Center, with a new type of rooming-in for the site, as a quasi-experimental opportunity to further clarify these relationships. 
The study will run in two modules: Recruitment for Module A will begin in the existing NICU and continue in the new NICU. The main focus here will be on the safety of the new environment with rooming-in and closer parent-child contact. The primary focus is the colonization rate with multi-resistant and highly pathogenic pathogens. Additonally, the frequency of transmission chains and possible infections in the treated patients in comparison between the new and old NICU and depending on rooming-in with one parent and with other parent-child pairs is of interest as well. Module B takes place in the new NICU and is exploratory in nature. The aim is to analyze the relationships between the development of the neonatal microbiome and immune system under finely granularly documented external influences (e.g. nutrition, antibiotics, probiotics, birth mode) by means of high-dimensional analysis with regard to the clinical course. In addition, the reciprocal influences between the child and parental microbiome as well as the microbial load of the environment are to be investigated. For this purpose, 100 parent-child pairs will be included. The patient microbiome will be analyzed from nasal and rectal swabs as well as stool samples. In addition, a quantitative analysis of immune cell populations from blood is carried out at several points in time. Particular attention is paid here to the highly efficient utilization of the biomaterial obtained (for clinical indications anyway), for which new methods (e.g. epigenetic immune cell analysis from dried blood) are used. In addition, nasal swabs and stool samples from the parents as well as environmental samples from the intensive care unit are analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Module A:
All admitted patients in the defined study period.

Module B:
For Module B, all premature infants under 32 weeks gestational age are included. In addition, newborns/preterm infants with a higher gestational age are included if an inpatient treatment period of at least 7 days has been reached. In addition, any parents who may have been admitted are also included (Rooming-In-Setting).
Exclusion criteria:
Missing declaration of consent.
